LESSON: INVERTEBRATES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 1.2: Invertebrates

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Invertebrates
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What are the common features of invertebrates?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify common invertebrates in the environment
2. practise precautions in handling invertebrates
3. describe the general characteristics of invertebrates
4. appreciate the importance of invertebrates in nature
5. identify main parts of the human circulatory system
6. describe functions of main parts of the human circulatory system

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Invertebrates

Teach
• Observe Invertebrates in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Invertebrates (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Invertebrates.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Invertebrates.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Invertebrates.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• identify common invertebrates in the environment
• practise precautions in handling invertebrates
• describe the general characteristics of invertebrates

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Invertebrates.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Invertebrates: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the common features of invertebrates?
2. What is the human circulatory system made up of?
3. What measures enhance a healthy human circulatory system?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• identify common invertebrates in the environment
• practise precautions in handling invertebrates
• describe the general characteristics of invertebrates
• appreciate the importance of invertebrates in nature

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
